_doc: What kind of file a file is, shown on every file a person sees (a badge: a picture, a word and a colour, so that someone who reads little or nothing still knows), and a word of caution before someone opens one they were sent (2026-10-17, from a suggestion in the project's Discord: say when a file is a program, a script, an archive and so on, and to scan it first). Read by the desktop app (src/net/file_risk.rs) and the website (web/shared/file-risk.js), the same way, from this one list. Not an antivirus: it reads a file's name and its first bytes. `kinds` deserve care; `named_as` are the kinds a name can claim, with which kinds of contents would make that claim a disguise; `unknown` is any other file. `level`: view (fine to look at: green), care (amber), danger (red), unknown (grey). `icon` names a drawing in `icons`, each a list of shapes on a 48 by 48 grid that both apps draw (rect [x,y,w,h], line [x1,y1,x2,y2], poly [x,y,...] open unless closed, circle [cx,cy,r]; fill fills it). `extensions` are lower case without the dot. `magic` is a file's first bytes in lower-case hex. Words: {ext} is the file's ending, {claimed} and {actual} are names from this file.

kinds.name: a program
kinds.label: Program
kinds.words: This is a program ({ext}). A program can do anything on your computer, like stealing your passwords or locking your files until you pay. Only open it if you trust the person who sent it, and check it with your antivirus first.

kinds.name: a script
kinds.label: Script
kinds.words: This is a script ({ext}). A script runs commands on your computer as soon as it is opened, and can do the same harm as a program, like stealing your passwords. Only open it if you trust the person who sent it, and check it with your antivirus first.

kinds.name: an archive
kinds.label: Archive
kinds.words: This is an archive ({ext}): a package holding other files. Nothing inside it has been checked. Check it with your antivirus before you open what it holds, and take care with any program inside.

kinds.name: a document that can carry macros
kinds.label: Macro document
kinds.words: This document can carry macros ({ext}): small programs that run inside it and can harm your computer. If it asks you to turn on macros or editing, say no, unless you trust the person who sent it.

kinds.name: a shortcut
kinds.label: Shortcut
kinds.words: This is a shortcut ({ext}). A shortcut can start a program or open a website without showing you which. Do not open it unless you trust the person who sent it.

kinds.name: a web page
kinds.label: Web page
kinds.words: This is a web page or markup file ({ext}). Opened, it runs in your web browser with its own scripts, and can show a fake sign-in page to steal your password. Do not open it unless you trust the person who sent it.

kinds.name: a Blender file
kinds.label: Blender file
kinds.words: Blender files can carry scripts: small programs that run inside Blender and can harm your computer. If Blender asks whether to run them, say no unless you trust the person who shared it.

disguised: This file is named like {claimed} ({ext}), but what is inside is {actual}. Do not open it. This is a trick: people who want to steal your passwords or money, or harm your computer, give harmful files the names of pictures, videos or documents so you will open them.
